extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers / authors submitting manuscripts to journals
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for authors on how to interpret and respond to peer review feedback—especially harsh or critical comments from the so-called 'Reviewer 2'—to improve a manuscript and navigate revision/editor interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of peer review / reviewers' responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is the bedrock of academic publishing, a meticulous process designed to ensure the quality and credibility of research before it reaches the wider audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers (referees) are experts responsible for testing ideas, scrutinizing hypotheses, and validating research findings to ensure research integrity. Their comments and recommendations are instrumental in guiding authors toward improved research quality and shaping the final published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer 2: Excessive criticism (stereotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer 2 is often seen as overly critical and uncompromising, passing caustic comments that can be offensive or discouraging for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize this stereotype as a common perception; anticipate blunt or harsh language and separate tone from substantive points. Use strategies below (stay calm, analyze feedback) to extract constructive elements even from caustic comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer 2: Lack of understanding (stereotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors sometimes believe that Reviewer 2 does not fully scrutinize the article and comprehend the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you suspect misunderstanding, clarify assumptions in the manuscript and, if needed, politely explain reasoning in your response letter. Consider whether additional explanation, framing, or citations would reduce misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer 2: Resistance to change (stereotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may perceive Reviewer 2 as resistant to accepting revisions, often falling back on their ‘boxed in’ understanding of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewer perspective reflects a conservative or narrowly framed view, present clear, evidence-based arguments for your approach and highlight how revisions address concerns while preserving the study’s aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer 2: Unnecessary or unreasonable revision requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Some comments insist on citing the reviewer’s work or request major revisions without proper reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify requests that lack justification. For unreasonable demands, provide a concise, polite rebuttal explaining why the change is unnecessary or infeasible, and cite supporting literature or constraints (e.g., scope, data availability). If appropriate, ask the editor for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the impact of harsh reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer 2’s often biased, unproductive, and harsh criticisms can have a detrimental impact, leading authors to doubt themselves or withdraw promising manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of potential negative effects on individuals and marginalized groups. Use editorial channels and professional support if comments cross into bias or harassment, and document harmful reviews if raising concerns with the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay calm and objective when reading reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotions can run high, but it’s crucial to remain calm and objective when reading comments from Reviewer 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pause for a day or two before responding to negative comments. Distance helps avoid defensive replies and allows a clearer assessment of which changes genuinely improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze feedback thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully analyze each comment and suggestion, considering how it can improve the quality of your research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate comments into actionable items, prioritize changes that strengthen validity, clarity, and rigor, and identify which suggestions are subjective or out of scope. Treat each reviewer point systematically in your response document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use feedback to enhance the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive criticism is invaluable in the pursuit of academic excellence, pushing authors to refine their work further.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace reviewer comments as opportunities for improvement—make necessary revisions that strengthen argumentation, methods, clarity, and presentation. Where you accept changes, indicate them clearly in your revision notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek clarification for unclear or conflicting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a comment is unclear or seems unreasonable, don’t hesitate to seek clarification from the editor or reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewers disagree, reflect on each comment and decide which to implement; if choices are unclear or contradictory, ask the editor to arbitrate or request more detail so you can revise appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in constructive dialogue via the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in constructive dialogue with Reviewer 2 through the editor if necessary, focusing on the research’s merit and improvement potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the editor as a mediator to communicate respectfully and professionally. Focus responses on evidence and manuscript improvement rather than personal disagreement. If persistent dispute remains after revisions, follow editorial advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond professionally and comprehensively to each comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that you are responding to each of the reviewer’s comments clearly without taking on a defensive tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide point-by-point responses explaining changes made or justified reasons for not making changes. Keep tone polite and evidence-based; if you cannot reach consensus, defer to the editor’s judgment after explaining your position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a growth mindset toward reviewer feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should view Reviewer 2’s comments as an opportunity for growth and improvement rather than an adversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframe criticism as a tool to deliver a more refined and rigorous paper. Maintain openness to revision while balancing scope and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolving norms: emphasize transparency, constructive feedback, and continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: As the academic publishing landscape evolves, both authors and reviewers need to adapt with an emphasis on transparency, constructive feedback, and continuous improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support norms and practices that promote clear, fair, and actionable reviews. When possible, model constructive reviewing behavior in your own reviews and advocate for editorial policies that reduce abusive or unhelpful reviewer practices.
